messages.author: bff58d77dc5c7cf4
messages.subject: Re: interactive plots?
parts:
Tom,

If all you are doing is plotting a linechart the GoogleVis LineChart is just the thing.
It needs to be embedded in a renderGvis call in server and htmlOutput in ui.

An example code is attached (note that this example is not terribly efficient, since
the read.table(ftp...) call is repeated when you switch between datasets. But I wrote this
before Joe Cheng tought me about global.R)

H.

messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Re: interactive plots?
parts:
Is there any desire to create an archive (or tutorials) of such packages/functions, to ease the search? It would be nice to have a catalog of sorts to answer, "I am going to add a heatmap, let's look at the list to see if anyone has made something cool for heatmaps yet!", or "What types of interactive line graphs are out there?"  As is, it feels like I have to get lucky to stumble upon a thread in which people are talking about it or in a google search. So I don't know what bases are already covered or if someone is planning on adding something in particular.  Most of the ones I have found seem pretty niche, pageable from googleVis seems to be the most broadly adaptable as a replacement for generic table output. There's also the "that's cool, but I have no idea of how they got their data in the format needed to use this" factor which has come up as well.

Just wishful thinking, is all.
